questions.prompt: Where are food materials stored in the cell?
questions.explanation: Food reserves are stored in the cytoplasm. Mitochondria release energy and the nucleus holds the DNA.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these is known as the "protein workbench" of the cell?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are where amino acids are joined into proteins.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these organelles sometimes acts as a "suicide bag"?
questions.explanation: Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes. If they burst they digest the cell, so they are called suicide bags.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The largest and most easily seen organelle within a eukaryotic cell is the ________.
questions.explanation: The nucleus is the largest and most easily seen organelle.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Another functional name for the nucleus is the ________.
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA, the cell's genetic information, so it is the information center.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Another descriptive nickname for the nucleus is the ________.
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the DNA, so it is called the information center of the cell.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The nucleus is also known as the ________.
questions.explanation: The energy house is the mitochondrion and the export center is the Golgi body. The nucleus is the information center.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: What is the function of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
options: Synthesizing and transporting lipids and steroid hormones
questions.explanation: Smooth ER has no ribosomes. It makes lipids and steroid hormones, while rough ER makes proteins.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Polysomes (polyribosomes) are groups of ________ lying freely or attached to membranes.
questions.explanation: A polysome is a string of ribosomes reading one mRNA at the same time.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The outer membrane of the nuclear envelope is continuous with which interior membrane system of the cytoplasm?
options: None of the above (it is the endoplasmic reticulum)
questions.explanation: The outer nuclear membrane is continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum, which is not listed.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Animal cells possess all of the following structures EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Plastids such as chloroplasts belong to plant cells and some protists.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set and ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ are barrel-shaped organelles found in cells of animals and most protists.
questions.explanation: Centrioles are small barrel-shaped organelles built from microtubules.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these carries hereditary material?
questions.explanation: Genes lie on chromosomes, which are made of DNA and protein.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which statement is FALSE about eukaryotic cells?
options: Their DNA is not associated with histones.
They contain more DNA than prokaryotes.
questions.explanation: Eukaryotic DNA is wrapped around histone proteins. The other statements are true.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The chromosome (nucleoid) of a prokaryote is found in the ________.
questions.explanation: A prokaryote has no nucleus. Its DNA lies in a region called the nucleoid.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The correspondence between the sequence of bases in DNA/RNA and the sequence of amino acids in a protein is known as the ________.
questions.explanation: The genetic code links base triplets (codons) to amino acids.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Mature mammalian erythrocytes (red blood cells) have how many nuclei?
questions.explanation: Mammalian red blood cells lose their nuclei as they mature.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Mammalian erythrocytes ________ their nuclei at maturity.
questions.explanation: Mammalian red cells lose the nucleus as they mature, leaving more room for haemoglobin.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Antonie van Leeuwenhoek lived as a scientist between ________.
questions.explanation: Leeuwenhoek lived from 1632 to 1723 and was the first to see bacteria and protozoa.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a general feature of living systems?
questions.explanation: General features of life include chemical composition, metabolism, development and response to the environment. Breathing is specific to some animals.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which feature of living systems aids nutrition?
questions.explanation: Metabolism covers the chemical reactions that handle food: digestion, absorption and use.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a biological macromolecule?
questions.explanation: Glucose is a monosaccharide, the small unit that builds carbohydrate polymers.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Macromolecules in living systems include ________.
questions.explanation: Proteins, carbohydrates, lipids and nucleic acids are the major biological macromolecules.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ are the monomeric subunits of protein macromolecules.
questions.explanation: Proteins are chains of amino acids.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Histology is the microscopic study of the ________ of cells and tissues.
questions.explanation: Histology is the study of the microscopic structure of cells and tissues.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: A common histological stain that stains the cytoplasm of a cell pink is ________.
questions.explanation: Eosin stains cytoplasm pink. Hematoxylin stains nuclei blue-purple.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: All of the following EXCEPT one are basic categories of animal tissues:
questions.explanation: The four basic animal tissues are epithelial, connective, muscle and nervous. Serous describes a type of secretion.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these statements is FALSE about cells?
options: They are the functional unit of life.
They are the fabric of life.
They are the smallest independent unit of life.
They are the basic organizational unit of life.
questions.explanation: All four statements are accepted descriptions of the cell, so the answer is probably E (none of the above), but it is not a standard textbook item.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: All four statements look true. Please confirm whether the key is E or whether one option was altered.

questions.prompt: All of the following EXCEPT one are general features of living systems:
questions.explanation: All four are general features of living systems.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: All four options are general features, so no option is the exception. The paper may have a missing option. Needs the original.

questions.prompt: Which of these carries hereditary material?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes carry the genes. Nucleoprotein (DNA + protein) is also defensible.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Chromosomes and nucleoprotein are both defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Freshwater zooplankton known as filter feeders are usually abundant in which months of the year?
questions.explanation: This depends on a local seasonal pattern that is not taught in a standard text.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Needs the key from the lecturer or course notes.

questions.prompt: Which of these statements is FALSE?
options: A cell is mainly composed of a nucleus and cytoplasm.
Mammalian red blood cells have no nucleus.
Liver cells (hepatocytes) occasionally have two nuclei.
Osteoclasts have seven or more nuclei.
questions.explanation: All four statements are accepted, so the key is probably E.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: All four look true. Please confirm the key.

questions.prompt: Carrier-mediated transport of molecules through the cell membrane using transport proteins embedded in the membrane is called ________.
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion uses carrier or channel proteins and moves molecules down their gradient.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set and ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Carrier-assisted transport of large molecules aided by transport proteins is referred to as ________.
questions.explanation: Transport proteins in the membrane carry molecules by facilitated diffusion.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these requires cellular energy (ATP)?
questions.explanation: Active transport moves molecules against the gradient and uses ATP.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ is a type of transport that does not require chemical energy.
questions.explanation: Passive transport follows the concentration gradient and needs no ATP.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The basic structure of the plasma membrane is a ________.
questions.explanation: The membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a passive transport process?
questions.explanation: Endocytosis and exocytosis need ATP. Facilitated diffusion does not.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which type of transport across the cell membrane does NOT rely solely on passive permeability along a concentration gradient?
questions.explanation: Endocytosis is a bulk transport that needs energy. The others are passive.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Bulk transport of material out of a cell is known as ________.
questions.explanation: Exocytosis moves material out in vesicles. Endocytosis brings it in.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set and ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The ________ acts as a gatekeeper regulating the entry and exit of substances involved in cell metabolism.
questions.explanation: The plasma membrane is selectively permeable and controls what enters and leaves.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: All biological membranes primarily contain ________.
questions.explanation: Biological membranes are mostly lipids and proteins.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ contains roughly 18% protein and 76% lipid.
questions.explanation: Myelin is about 80% lipid, which is why it insulates nerve fibres.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Depolymerization is inhibited in microtubules through the binding of ________ to each end.
questions.explanation: A GTP cap at the end of a microtubule stops it from depolymerizing.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ proteins move cellular organelles toward the center (minus end) of the cell.
questions.explanation: Dyneins walk toward the minus end of microtubules, near the centre. Kinesins walk toward the plus end.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which phase of cell division has the chromosomes lining up at the equator of the spindle?
questions.explanation: In metaphase the chromosomes align on the metaphase plate at the cell equator.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: A pair of centrioles is referred to as a ________.
questions.explanation: A centrosome is a pair of centrioles with surrounding material that organises the spindle.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ is typically the longest phase in mitosis.
questions.explanation: Prophase is usually the longest stage of mitosis.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Synapsis allows for ________.
questions.explanation: Synapsis pairs homologous chromosomes so that crossing over can exchange genetic material.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Chromosomes are replicated during the ________ phase of interphase.
questions.explanation: DNA is copied in the S (synthesis) phase.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: In a diploid human somatic cell after S phase, how many chromatids are present?
questions.explanation: There are still 46 chromosomes but each has two sister chromatids, so 92 chromatids.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Before cell division, each chromosome replicates to produce two identical ________.
questions.explanation: Replication gives two identical sister chromatids joined at the centromere.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: A large proteinaceous structure that forms between aligned homologous chromosomes during meiotic prophase is the ________.
questions.explanation: The synaptonemal complex holds homologues together during synapsis.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: A point of contact where crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids is called a ________.
questions.explanation: A chiasma is the X-shaped point where non-sister chromatids have crossed over.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Crossing over takes place at which stage of meiosis?
questions.explanation: Crossing over takes place in prophase I (pachytene).
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT part of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Interphase is the stage before mitosis. Mitosis is prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a biological significance of mitosis?
questions.explanation: Genetic variation comes from meiosis. Mitosis gives genetically identical cells.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which division produces a large ootid (ovum) and a very small second polar body?
questions.explanation: The second meiotic division splits the secondary oocyte into a large ootid and a small second polar body.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The following processes occur in telophase EXCEPT:
options: chromatids reach the polar ends of the spindle fibers
questions.explanation: Centrioles replicate in interphase (S phase), not telophase. Chromatids also become densely packed in prophase, not telophase.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Both options B and C can be argued as not happening in telophase. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Independent assortment of chromosomes and crossing over cause ________.
questions.explanation: Both genetic variation and genetic recombination are accepted.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Options B and C are both defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: The transmission of traits from parents to their offspring is referred to as ________.
questions.explanation: Heredity is the passing of traits from parents to offspring.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: DNA contains ________.
questions.explanation: The DNA backbone is made of deoxyribose sugar joined by phosphate groups.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: DNA is made up of linear chains of subunits known as ________.
questions.explanation: The subunits of DNA are nucleotides, each with a sugar, a phosphate and a base.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ is a very long, linear chain of nucleotides, each containing a sugar-phosphate backbone and a nitrogenous base.
questions.explanation: The long chain of nucleotides is DNA. Adenine, cytosine and guanine are only bases.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Genes carried on the sex chromosomes are said to be ________.
questions.explanation: Genes on the sex chromosomes are sex-linked.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Traits that appear in the F1 generation when parents with different traits are crossed are said to be ________.
questions.explanation: The trait that appears in F1 is dominant. The hidden one is recessive.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.sourceNote: Original wording: "Traits transmitted unchanged from parents to the F1 generation".

questions.prompt: All of the following are sex-linked or sex-influenced EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Height is controlled by many genes on autosomes and is not sex-linked.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: How many pairs of chromosomes are present in human somatic cells?
questions.explanation: Human somatic cells have 46 chromosomes, which is 23 pairs.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The axial and appendicular skeletons in humans consist of ________ and ________ bones respectively.
questions.explanation: The axial skeleton has 80 bones and the appendicular skeleton has 126, making 206 in total.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Sex-linked traits/genes include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Colour blindness and hemophilia are X-linked. Premature baldness is sex-influenced and myopia is not sex-linked.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Myopia and premature baldness are both arguably not sex-linked. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Traits carried by genes on the sex chromosomes include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Albinism is autosomal. Premature baldness is sex-influenced, not strictly sex-linked.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Options D and E are both arguably not sex-linked. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Which of these hormones is a steroid hormone?
questions.explanation: Testosterone and estrogen are both steroid hormones.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Options C and E are both correct. Needs the original single answer.

questions.prompt: How many functional daughter cells (ova) are produced at the end of oogenesis from a primary oocyte?
questions.explanation: One primary oocyte gives one functional ovum and polar bodies.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The ________ and ________ control spermatogenesis.
questions.explanation: The hypothalamus releases GnRH and the anterior pituitary releases FSH and LH.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.sourceNote: Options (a) and (d) were identical in the typed paper; one copy removed.

questions.prompt: How many daughter cells are produced at the end of spermatogenesis from a primary spermatocyte?
questions.explanation: One primary spermatocyte gives four spermatids and so four sperm.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: In humans, sperm can only fertilize the secondary oocyte after spending how long in the female reproductive tract (capacitation)?
questions.explanation: Capacitation takes a few hours.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Sperm usually spend ________ hours in the female genital tract before fertilizing the oocyte.
questions.explanation: Human sperm need about 7 hours of capacitation in the female tract.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The activating process of sperm inside the female genital tract before fertilization is known as ________.
questions.explanation: Capacitation makes sperm able to fertilize an egg.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The human sperm production rate is approximately ________.
questions.explanation: A man makes roughly 120 million sperm per day.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: ________ is responsible for inhibiting and regulating spermatogenesis.
questions.explanation: Inhibin from the Sertoli cells slows FSH release and so regulates spermatogenesis.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Cleavage results in the formation of a mass of cells called a ________.
questions.explanation: Cleavage divides the zygote into a ball of cells, the blastula.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The visible sign of the cortical reaction is ________.
options: thickening/elevation of the vitelline membrane (fertilization membrane)
questions.explanation: After a sperm enters, the vitelline membrane lifts and hardens into the fertilization membrane.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: All of the following are types of cleavage pattern based on yolk content EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Radial cleavage describes the plane of division, not the yolk content.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: What type of cleavage results when an egg has little or no yolk?
questions.explanation: A yolk-poor egg divides completely and equally (holoblastic).
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Cleavage in an egg with little or no yolk is known as ________ cleavage.
questions.explanation: Little yolk allows the whole egg to divide, which is holoblastic cleavage.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Morphogenetic movement transforms the hollow spherical blastula into a ________.
questions.explanation: Gastrulation reshapes the blastula into the gastrula.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Mollusks, annelids, nemerteans and some flatworms undergo which type of cleavage?
questions.explanation: These spiralian animals show spiral cleavage.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Primary germ layers of triploblastic animals include all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: All three layers (ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm) are present, so none is the exception.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The epidermis is derived from which embryological germ layer?
questions.explanation: The epidermis comes from ectoderm.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these tissues are derived from the mesoderm?
questions.explanation: Connective and muscle tissue come from mesoderm. Nervous tissue comes from ectoderm.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Epithelial tissues can be derived from which embryological germ layer(s)?
questions.explanation: Epithelia arise from ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The circulatory system is formed from the ________.
questions.explanation: The heart, blood and blood vessels develop from mesoderm.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these is formed from the mesoderm?
questions.explanation: The excretory system develops from mesoderm. The liver is endodermal and receptors and nose are ectodermal.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The ________ is a transitory endocrine gland formed from the ruptured follicle that secretes progesterone and estrogen.
questions.explanation: After ovulation the ruptured follicle becomes the corpus luteum.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: When does the production of oogonia occur in human females?
questions.explanation: Oogonia form and divide during fetal development.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which is NOT a gonadotropin?

questions.prompt: In a typical 28-day cycle, how many days does it take for the corpus luteum to start degenerating if fertilization fails to occur?
questions.explanation: The corpus luteum lasts about 10–14 days after ovulation. Books differ.

questions.prompt: At birth, approximately how many follicles are present in a human ovary?
questions.explanation: Textbooks give 1–2 million follicles at birth.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Both 1 million and 2 million are cited. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Which statement is NOT true?
options: Spermatogenesis begins from primordial germ cells.
Oogenesis begins from germinal epithelial cells.
Spermatogenesis is controlled by the hypothalamus and anterior pituitary gland working together.
questions.explanation: A and C are standard statements. B is a debated way of describing oogenesis.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which are core unifying theories that guide the study of zoology?
questions.explanation: Evolution, inheritance and the chromosomal theory are all given as unifying theories in different texts.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: More than one combination can be argued. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: The ________ is a derivative of the mesoderm.
questions.explanation: The notochord and much of the skull are mesodermal.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Notochord and skull are both defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Stratified squamous epithelium ________.
options: is located in the male urethra
lines the esophagus, mouth and vagina
lines the air sacs of the lungs
questions.explanation: Stratified squamous epithelium resists wear and lines the mouth, oesophagus and vagina.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: A type of exocrine gland in which secretory products are released without damaging the cell is a ________.
questions.explanation: Merocrine glands release secretions by exocytosis and the cell stays intact.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: An example of a holocrine gland is the ________.
questions.explanation: Sebaceous gland cells break down completely to form sebum.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these types of epithelium has flattened cells?
questions.explanation: Squamous cells are flat.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a function of epithelial tissue?
questions.explanation: Epithelia protect, secrete and reduce friction.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which cells are unicellular glands found among the columnar cells of the intestine and secrete mucus?
questions.explanation: Goblet cells are single mucus-secreting cells between intestinal columnar cells.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: What are the shape and position of the nucleus in simple cuboidal epithelial cells?
options: Elongated and located near the base
Spherical and located near the base
questions.explanation: Cuboidal cells have a round nucleus in the centre. Columnar cells have an oval nucleus near the base.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which type of simple epithelium has a spherical nucleus positioned at the center of each cell?
questions.explanation: Cuboidal cells have a central spherical nucleus.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Sublingual glands are predominantly ________ in nature.
questions.explanation: Sublingual glands are mainly mucous.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) and ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of these glands predominantly contains mucous acini?
questions.explanation: The sublingual glands are mainly mucous. The parotid and pancreas are serous.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: One or more layers of cells covering the outer surface or lining the hollow spaces of the body are referred to as ________.
questions.explanation: This is the definition of epithelial tissue.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following glands secretes via exocytosis?
questions.explanation: Salivary glands are merocrine and release their products by exocytosis. Sebaceous and Meibomian glands are holocrine.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic feature of epithelial tissue?
questions.explanation: Epithelia have no blood vessels (avascular) and are fed by diffusion from the tissue below.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which cell surface modification increases the surface area of a cell without increasing its size?
questions.explanation: Microvilli are tiny finger-like folds that increase the absorptive surface.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: In glands, epithelial tissue is specialized to secrete specific chemical substances such as ________.
questions.explanation: Gland epithelium secretes enzymes, hormones and lubricating fluids such as mucus.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set and ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The sweat glands located in the armpit (axilla) and genital area are called ________.
questions.explanation: Apocrine sweat glands are in the armpit and genital areas.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which epithelial type best identifies the kind that lines the stomach and intestine?
questions.explanation: Simple columnar epithelium lines the stomach and intestine for secretion and absorption.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which secretion mechanism discharges the whole cell into the lumen as the cell degenerates?
questions.explanation: In holocrine secretion the entire cell breaks up and becomes the secretion.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: What type of gland releases its secretion into the surrounding tissue and bloodstream rather than through a duct?
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into the tissue fluid and blood.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The intense basophilia in the basal region of serous cells results from a large accumulation of ________ and ________.
options: rough endoplasmic reticulum and free ribosomes
rough endoplasmic reticulum and free lysosomes
questions.explanation: Serous cells make a lot of protein, so they are packed with rough ER and ribosomes, which stain with basic dyes.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The nuclei of serous cells are ________ located, while those of mucous cells are ________ located.
questions.explanation: Serous cells have round, central nuclei. Mucous cells have flattened nuclei pushed to the base.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The nuclei of mucous cells are ________ located.
questions.explanation: Mucous cells have a flattened nucleus pushed to the base by mucus droplets.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The nuclei of serous cells are ________ located.
questions.explanation: Serous cells have a round nucleus in the central region.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The tarsal (Meibomian) glands of the eyelid use what type of secretion mechanism?
questions.explanation: Meibomian glands are modified sebaceous glands and are holocrine.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: All epithelial tissues are supported by a ________ of variable thickness.
questions.explanation: Epithelia rest on a basement membrane.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which of the following sweat gland secretions is associated with pheromonal or sexual attraction?
questions.explanation: Apocrine gland secretions carry body odour and pheromones.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The crypts of Lieberkühn are a type of ________.
questions.explanation: The intestinal crypts are simple straight tubular glands.
questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: All of the following EXCEPT one are examples of exocrine glands according to the nature of their secretions:
questions.explanation: "Acinar" describes the shape of a gland, not what it secretes.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Apocrine secretion is associated with ________.
questions.explanation: In apocrine secretion the tip of the cell is pinched off with the secretion, as in the mammary gland.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Glands in which part of the cell cytoplasm is pinched off with the secretion are called ________ glands.
questions.explanation: Apocrine glands lose a piece of the apical cytoplasm with the secretion.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Ceruminous glands are located in the ________.
questions.explanation: Ceruminous glands in the ear canal make earwax.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Which type of epithelium is found lining the uterus?
questions.explanation: The endometrium has simple columnar epithelium with some ciliated cells.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Options A and B are both defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: In which of these glands do secretions reach target cells through the extracellular space/tissue fluid?
questions.explanation: Endocrine glands release into the tissue fluid and then the blood. Paracrine signals act through the tissue fluid.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: Endocrine and paracrine are both defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Exocytosis occurs in ________.
questions.explanation: Exocytosis occurs in endocrine and merocrine (exocrine) secretion.
questions.source: ZOO 101, June 2020 (2018/2019 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: More than one option is defensible. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: Lining epithelia are classified based on all of the following EXCEPT:

questions.source: ZOO 101 practice set (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)
questions.reviewNote: All three listed bases are used, so the intended exception is unclear. Needs the key.

questions.prompt: The main structural component of the dermis is a protein called ________.
questions.explanation: Collagen forms most of the dermis.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The ligamentum flavum is an example of ________ connective tissue.
questions.explanation: The ligamentum flavum is rich in elastic fibres and is dense elastic connective tissue.

questions.prompt: The matrix of connective tissues is made up of ________.
questions.explanation: The matrix is ground substance plus fibres.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The most common resident cell type in connective tissues is the ________.
questions.explanation: Fibroblasts are the most common resident cell and make the fibres and ground substance.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Macrophages arise from precursor cells called ________.
questions.explanation: Monocytes leave the blood and become macrophages.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Monocytes are precursor cells of which of the following connective tissue cells?

questions.prompt: Which type of collagen is an important structural component of the basal lamina?

questions.prompt: Coarse collagen fibers in connective tissues are formed mainly from which collagen type?

questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: The primary function of collagen fibers is to add ________ to connective tissues.
questions.explanation: Collagen resists pulling and gives tensile strength.
questions.source: ZOO 101, December 2022 (2020/2021 session) (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Adipocytes are grouped into which category of connective tissue cells?
questions.explanation: Adipocytes stay in place and are fixed cells.
questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Bone is an example of ________.
questions.explanation: Bone is a specialised connective tissue.

questions.prompt: Cartilage is a form of ________ connective tissue with collagenous fibers embedded in a ________ matrix.

questions.source: ZOO 101, 2017/2018 session (typed; no answer key supplied, so answers are set from standard zoology and histology textbooks)

questions.prompt: Partly movable (cartilaginous) joints are found in the ________.

questions.prompt: The highly viscous character of the ground substance of connective tissues is ensured by ________.

questions.prompt: The arrangement of actin and myosin filaments in a skeletal muscle fiber is organized into a ________.

questions.prompt: The type of neuron that conducts impulses from the central nervous system to effector organs is a ________.

questions.prompt: The epineurium is a sheath of dense connective tissue that surrounds a ________.

questions.prompt: The junctions where nerve cells functionally connect to one another are called ________.

questions.prompt: Merkel cells in the skin function as ________.

questions.prompt: Which of the following tissues are referred to as excitable tissues?
